review_question: Among women and adolescents receiving contraceptive services, does advance provision of emergency contraceptive pills increase subsequent emergency contraceptive pill use compared with standard or on-demand access?

pico.population: Women or adolescents at risk of pregnancy receiving contraceptive services
pico.intervention_or_exposure: Advance provision of emergency contraceptive pills
pico.comparator: Standard or on-demand emergency contraceptive pill access
pico.outcome: Any subsequent emergency contraceptive pill use

outcome.description: Any subsequent emergency contraceptive pill use

targets.comparison: Advance provision of emergency contraceptive pills versus standard or on-demand access
targets.population_or_subgroup: Women or adolescents at risk of pregnancy receiving contraceptive services

timepoint_policy.rule: Capture every source-supported participant-level record of one-or-more emergency contraceptive pill use from 6 through 12 months. Preserve the precise cohort, analysis denominator, and follow-up wording.

candidate_capture_policy.record_scope: Capture complete source-supported arm-level binary records, including linked reports where the source has one; defer cohort de-duplication and record choice to analysis.

targets.quantitative_use_policy: Extract only participant event counts paired with source-declared denominators in both groups, the outcome definition, cohort, follow-up duration, and verified primary-source locator. Do not reconstruct counts from rounded percentages, use a subgroup denominator as an all-randomized denominator, or copy a review forest-plot value. A total-minus-zero-use derivation is permitted only where both cells come from the same source table.

output_contract.effect_unit: one source-reported arm-level binary emergency-contraception-use outcome
